To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the levels of components involved in GSH synthesis, degradation and conjugation are altered in Ames dwarf mice.

(1) the levels of glutamate-cysteiglycine ligase (GCL), the rate limiting enzyme in GSH synthesis, were increased in dwarf mice, which is likely responsible for the increased levels of GSH; (2) the activity of gamma-glucamyltransferase (GGT), which catalyzes the degradation of GSH, is lower in dwarf mice; (3) the activity of GST, which utilizes GSH, is higher in dwarf mice
the Ames dwarf mouse exhibits elevated glutathione synthesis and utilization and reduced glutathione degradation, which may contribute to the extended longevity of this animal model of longevity.

GGT and GST are key enzymes in the metabolism of glutathione and are involved in the regulation of the cellular redox state.

GGT activity is lower in tissues of long-living dwarf mice and that this may contribute to their increased longevity by reducing oxidative stress.
